question_text: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents after he was bitten by a friend's cat while playing at their house. The patient reports moderate pain of the right hand and wrist but has full range of motion and strength. He is up to date on his vaccinations and is generally healthy. His vitals are unremarkable. Physical exam reveals a deep puncture wound that is actively bleeding. The wound is irrigated and a dressing is applied. Which of the following is appropriate management of this patient?

        ### Question
        A 12-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents after he was bitten by a friend's cat while playing at their house. The patient reports moderate pain of the right hand and wrist but has full range of motion and strength. He is up to date on his vaccinations and is generally healthy. His vitals are unremarkable. Physical exam reveals a deep puncture wound that is actively bleeding. The wound is irrigated and a dressing is applied. Which of the following is appropriate management of this patient?

        ### Options
        opa. Ampicillin-sulbactam and surgical debridement
opb. Ampicillin-sulbactam, surgical debridgment, and laceration closure
opc. Amoxicillin-clavulanate
opd. Amoxicillin-clavulanate and laceration closure
ope. Laceration closure

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Cat bite -> potential introduction of bacteria into the wound -> risk of infection -> 80% CHAIN: Deep puncture wound -> increased risk of infection due to difficulty in cleaning and potential for bacteria to be trapped -> 75% CHAIN: Irrigation of the wound -> removal of debris and bacteria -> decreased risk of infection -> 70% CHAIN: Application of dressing -> protection of the wound from external contaminants -> reduced risk of infection -> 70% CHAIN: Ampicillin-sulbactam administration -> broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage -> targeting potential bacterial pathogens -> 80% CHAIN: Surgical debridement -> removal of damaged tissue and foreign material -> improved wound healing -> 75% CHAIN: Laceration closure -> sealing the wound to promote healing and reduce infection risk -> 80%
